rationale: X correctly rejects the reorder and covers every requested contract: strict additions raise before mutation, `strict: true` maps to `ActiveModel::StrictValidationFailed`, custom exception classes are raised with the full message, and ordinary `add` appends and returns the `ActiveModel::Error`. These claims match `activemodel/lib/active_model/errors.rb:321-352`, the strict validation tests at `activemodel/test/cases/validations_test.rb:396-447`, and the normal return test at `activemodel/test/cases/errors_test.rb:227-234`. Its investigation was sufficient and its review comment is concise, autonomous, and conclusion-first.

strengths.summary: Directly rebuts the proposed inspect-after-rescue rationale by explaining why collection lookup is not a sound substitute for an exception payload.
strengths.evidence: X notes that strict `add` has no return value and that retrieving `errors.last` after rescue is ambiguous when errors were already recorded. This follows from the append-only normal path in `activemodel/lib/active_model/errors.rb:350-352` and is a useful practical consequence stated more explicitly than in the references.
